title: entity_bible
description: Persistent entities a production must keep identical across generated clips. Scene plans and prompts reference entities by entity_id so identity is stated once and cited everywhere, instead of being re-described (and re-invented) per beat. Covers process subjects (tools, containers, ingredients, work surfaces) and narrative subjects (characters, clothing, props, locations, vehicles) with the same shape.

entity_id.description: Stable handle cited by scene plans and prompts, e.g. working_glass.

visual_description.description: One paragraph a generator can render from. Concrete and discriminating: what makes THIS one recognisable, not a category description.

identity_constraints.description: What must be true in every frame this entity appears in.

continuity_constraints.description: What must hold ACROSS clips — the cross-boundary rules.

allowed_changes.description: Changes that are part of the story (a glass filling, a shirt getting wet). Without this an entity reads as frozen and legitimate transformation looks like a defect.

forbidden_changes.description: Changes that are defects (silhouette shifts, ingredient identity swaps, teleportation).

first_introduced_in.description: Act or beat id where a hand/camera introduces it. An entity with no introduction is the un-introduced-object defect.

global_forbidden_changes.description: Rules applying to every entity, e.g. nothing appears without a hand introducing it.
